captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/26_simmim, specifically its Swin-B step 1 (models/simmim_swinb.py, data/simmim_dataset.py, train_step1_swinb.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Xie et al. (2022) SimMIM, following microsoft/SimMIM. The step-1 code builds timm's SwinTransformer from scratch (measured: the `transformers` package appears only in a docstring note about HuggingFace pretrained weights and is never imported), so this ports self-contained and needs only timm. The port keeps the capture directory numbering (26) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: SimMIM: A Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling
paper.authors: Xie, Zhang, Cao, Lin, Bao, Yao, Dai, Hu

scope: The Swin-B step 1 is ported: images are patch-embedded by a Swin encoder; a random block of patch tokens (mask units of 32x32 pixels = 8x8 Swin patches, 60% masked) is replaced by a learned mask token; the full token grid is encoded by Swin; a 1x1 conv + PixelShuffle decoder reconstructs pixels; an L1 loss is taken only on the masked pixels. AdamW under a per-iteration schedule (linear warmup then a multistep decay), the base LR optionally scaled by the global batch size; gradient-norm clipping. The capture's step 2 (ViT) is EXCLUDED, as in every port.
encoder: encoder.pt is the bare Swin encoder (encoder.*, the prefix stripped so it loads straight into a plain timm SwinTransformer): the patch embed, the Swin stages and the final norm, producing the mean-pooled feature (encoder_dim; 1024 for Swin-B). The learned mask token (mask_token) and the reconstruction decoder (decoder.*) are training machinery and are excluded -- the standard SSL convention of probing the encoder.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the Swin encoder's mean-pooled forward_features (encoder_dim), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation -- the same normalisation SimMIM trains with). The capture's own SimMIM eval standardises the cached features (zero mean / unit std) then fits a linear head; this port follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own head, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.
rewritten_during_the_port: only the Swin-B step 1 is ported; the capture's step 2 (ViT) is excluded, as in every port

timm supplies the SwinTransformer (built from scratch, no pretrained download, so the run stays hermetic); the transformers package listed in the capture's requirements.txt is docstring-only and never imported (measured), so it is not a dependency of this port
build_swin_encoder is a single construction path shared by the SimMIM model and the linear-eval loader, so the encoder is built one way
img_size and the Swin dims are threaded so a small hermetic CPU smoke runs a tiny 2-stage Swin at a lower resolution
the mask generator, the mask-token replacement, the Conv+PixelShuffle decoder and the masked-pixel L1 loss are kept faithfully (all torch); step 1 uses patch-grid masks
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the capture called .cuda())
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch); the DataLoader gets a seeded generator

the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel, the AMP autocast/GradScaler and TensorBoard/tqdm so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32; the per-iteration warmup + multistep LR schedule and the global-batch LR scaling are kept
